summary: This is a Docker Compose configuration file that sets up a Joomla website with a MySQL database. It defines two services that will run in containers: a Joomla web application server and a MySQL database server. The services are linked together so Joomla can communicate with its database, and both services persist their data to folders on your computer.

explanations.6: The %%name=kingsbridge%% is a template variable that will be replaced with an actual name (defaulting to 'kingsbridge') when this file is processed — it's used to give the container a unique identifier.
explanations.9: The %%port=8080%% is another template variable that lets you specify which port on your computer maps to port 80 inside the container; if not set, it defaults to 8080.
explanations.12: The %%dbPassword=example%% is a template variable for the database password — it has a default value of 'example' but should be customized for security.
explanations.15: The 'condition: service_healthy' means Joomla won't start until the database reports back that it's healthy and ready to accept connections.
explanations.16: The ${UID:-1000}:${GID:-1000} syntax means use your system's user ID and group ID if available, otherwise default to 1000 — this ensures the container runs with proper file permissions.
explanations.27: This healthcheck command repeatedly tests whether MySQL is running and responding by pinging it; if it succeeds, Docker knows the database is ready.
explanations.28: The timeout of 20 seconds means each healthcheck attempt will wait up to 20 seconds for a response before deciding it failed.
explanations.29: Retries of 10 means Docker will try the healthcheck up to 10 times before giving up and marking the database as unhealthy.
